title: Ukraine strikes Ilsky refinery in Krasnodar — 3 killed, refinery halts; strike lands amid Trump-brokered energy ceasefire push
detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Ilsky oil refinery (KNGK-INPZ LLC) in Krasnodar Krai's Seversky District overnight Sept 25-26, hitting three primary oil-processing units and a tank farm and forcing the roughly 6.6-million-tonne/year plant to suspend operations — at least the 17th strike on the facility since the start of the full-scale war. Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratiev confirmed fires at the refinery and at two other enterprises in the district, and reported fatalities; Bloomberg, Kyiv Post and Time News put the toll at three killed and two injured, with drone debris also damaging a nearby residential building. Ukraine's General Staff, crediting the 1st Separate Center of Unmanned Systems Forces and the 414th Unmanned Systems Brigade ('Madyar's Birds'), called the strike an exercise of Ukraine's Article 51 right to self-defense; the refinery — a target distinct from the Perm and Novoshakhtinsk plants hit the previous day — supplies southern Russia's civilian and military fuel market. The strike came days after President Trump pressed both sides in New York for a bilateral 'energy ceasefire,' which Zelensky said Kyiv was ready to accept if Russia reciprocated; the Kremlin has not agreed to a full halt, and this strike — like a reported Russian barrage of 40+ drones on Ukraine hours after Trump touted the truce — suggests the proposal is not yet holding on either side.
